newsitem.title: UK: Bunker demand helps lift Euro fuel oil barges.
newsitem.headline: Bunker demand helps lift Euro fuel oil barges.

text.p: Post-holiday bunker demand pushed European high sulphur fuel barge prices up $1 on Tuesday but fuel cargo business was thin, traders said.

Barge deals were seen at $84.50 and $85 in Rotterdam, with $86 done in Antwerp. Some 30,000 tonnes of bunker demand was noted in Rotterdam as business returned to more normal levels after the long weekend.
"Pent-up demand has been released after the break and right now there are more buyers than sellers," said one trader.

Low sulphur prices held firm at around the $95 a tonne level set by last Friday's cargo deal. Traders were believed trying to combine parcels and find vessels that will allow the U.S. arbitrage to work.
Offers of cracked Russian fuel oil into the utility market suggested supplies of Russian material from St. Petersburg were starting to come through, though not yet at prices deemed competitive.
Straight-run values were steady, with end-May and early June material on offer.
